issues.t: Timing belt pulley or tensioner failure ruins the engine
issues.sym: A squeal, chirp or grinding from the front of the engine, then sudden stalling, often at highway speed. The engine may not restart, and it can be badly damaged.
issues.why: The timing belt idler and tensioner pulleys and the water pump (which the timing belt drives) can fail. When a pulley seizes or the belt jumps, the valves hit the pistons. GM ran a special policy and a customer satisfaction program to replace these parts, and parts were back-ordered for a time.
issues.next: If the belt and pulleys have no record of being replaced, have them, the water pump and the tensioner done now as one job, and do not wait for 100,000 miles. A squeal from the belt area means stop driving and get it checked.

issues.t: Stalls while driving and won't restart (crankshaft sensor)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, at low or highway speed, and may not restart until it cools down. There is often no warning light.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor is a common cause, according to RepairPal, and GM revised its diagnostic code P0335 for these cars. Owners report many stalls that dealers could not repeat.
issues.next: Stalling in traffic is a safety risk. Have the crankshaft sensor and its wiring tested, and ask for the codes to be read right after a stall happens.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the engine oil cooler
issues.sym: Coolant level drops, oil looks milky or coolant looks oily, or there are drips near the oil filter area.
issues.why: The oil cooler sits in the engine's coolant path, and its cover seal can leak. GM bulletin 200601 covers coolant leaks at the oil cooler cover. RepairPal lists coolant and oil leaks as the top Catera complaint.
issues.next: Check the oil and coolant for mixing. If they have mixed, have the cooler resealed and both fluids flushed soon, since oily coolant and watery oil both damage the engine.

issues.t: Coolant loss and overheating
issues.sym: The low coolant light comes on, the temperature gauge rises, coolant has to be added often, or steam comes from under the hood.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin covering coolant loss, low coolant warnings and overheating on these cars, plus a revised thermostat installation procedure. Owners also report water pump, hose and head gasket failures.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge goes into the red. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak before the engine overheats and the head gaskets fail.

issues.t: Temperature gauge reads hot when the engine is not overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge swings into the red or the overheat light comes on, but the engine is not actually running hot.
issues.why: GM bulletin 01-06-02-005 covers a false high temperature reading on these cars.
issues.next: Do not assume it is false; check the coolant level and look for steam first. If everything is normal, have the coolant temperature sensor and gauge checked.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or shifting badly
issues.sym: Slipping, delayed or harsh shifts, the car stuck in one gear, or a warning light. Owners report failures around 60,000-85,000 miles.
issues.why: The 4L30-E automatic has a history of internal wear and failure in the Catera. GM issued a service policy procedure for this transmission.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or stays in one gear, drive gently and get a transmission diagnosis before it fails completely.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) separates
issues.sym: A wobble or vibration from the engine belt pulley, a squeal, a belt thrown off, or loss of power steering and charging.
issues.why: The rubber bond between the hub and the outer ring of the crankshaft pulley can fail on the 3.0L V6. GM issued bulletins to inspect and replace it.
issues.next: Have the crankshaft pulley inspected. If it wobbles, replace it soon, since a thrown belt stops the alternator and power steering.

issues.t: Check engine light from a cracked air injection hose
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0411, sometimes with a hissing noise at startup.
issues.why: The secondary air injection hose can crack or develop a hole between its valves. GM ran a campaign and issued several bulletins on this hose.
issues.next: Have the hose inspected and replaced. It usually does not hurt how the car drives but will fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the valve cover and timing cover
issues.sym: Oil seeping on the top or front of the engine, a burning oil smell, or oil drips.
issues.why: Valve cover gasket leaks are a common Catera repair, and GM issued a bulletin for oil leaks from the engine timing cover.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Oil dripping on the exhaust can smoke and smell, and oil soaking the timing belt can shorten its life.

issues.t: Heater control valve leaks coolant
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, coolant dripping near the back of the engine, or heat that does not change properly.
issues.why: RepairPal lists leaking hot water control valves as a known Catera problem.
issues.next: Have the valve and its hoses checked when tracing any coolant leak.

issues.t: Hesitation or rough running fixed by a computer update
issues.sym: Hesitation, stumbling or rough running that no part replacement seems to fix.
issues.why: RepairPal reports that reprogramming the engine computer fixes drivability problems on these cars.
issues.next: Ask a Cadillac dealer or well-equipped shop to check for the latest engine computer software before replacing parts.

issues.t: Car pulls right and wears the front tires
issues.sym: The car drifts or pulls to the right, and the inside edges of the front tires wear fast.
issues.why: GM bulletin 81-31-02 covers lead right and inner tire wear on cars built before a certain VIN. Owners report replacing tires often.
issues.next: Get a full alignment from a shop that knows the bulletin, and check the tires for uneven wear.

issues.t: Heated seat overheats and burns the seat
issues.sym: A burning smell from the seat, the seat getting too hot, or a burn hole in the seat cushion.
issues.why: Owners report seat heating elements overheating and burning through the upholstery.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater if it ever feels too hot or you smell burning. Have the heating pad and switch checked or disconnected.

issues.t: Headlight aim adjusters break and lenses yellow
issues.sym: The headlights point the wrong way and cannot be adjusted, or the plastic lenses turn yellow and dim.
issues.why: The headlight assembly and its aiming parts break on many Cateras. CarComplaints lists headlight assembly breakage as a top problem.
issues.next: Have a shop check whether the adjusters can be repaired. Often the full headlight unit has to be replaced.

issues.t: ABS and traction control warning lights
issues.sym: The ABS or traction control lights come on, sometimes repeatedly after repairs, or the brakes feel odd.
issues.why: Owners report ABS and traction control faults and repeat warnings on these cars.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal braking still works, but get it fixed so the antilock system works in an emergency.

issues.t: Key is hard to remove from the ignition
issues.sym: The key will not come out of the ignition easily after you turn the car off.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for keys that are hard to remove from the ignition lock cylinder.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in Park. If it keeps happening, have the lock cylinder checked.

issues.t: Airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag light stays on after starting the car.
issues.why: GM bulletin 4573 covers the airbag light coming on with code 52 stored in the airbag module. Owners also report the light returning after a module change.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The airbags may not work while the light is on, so do not ignore it.

issues.t: Climate control display goes blank
issues.sym: The climate control panel goes blank and stops working, then may come back.
issues.why: GM bulletin 81-83-11 covers an intermittently blank and inoperative climate control head.
issues.next: Have the climate control unit and its connections checked.

issues.t: Radio dead and A/C won't engage
issues.sym: The radio does not work with the key on, and the A/C compressor does not turn on.
issues.why: GM bulletin 01317 covers this combination with communication code U1255.
issues.next: Ask a shop to read the body and radio codes and check the bulletin.

issues.t: Radio static from the rear window defogger
issues.sym: Static or buzzing on the radio when the rear defogger is on, or some defogger lines do not clear.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for radio interference from the rear defogger and for broken defogger grid lines.
issues.next: Have the defogger grid tabs and lines repaired.

issues.t: Steering column squeak when turning
issues.sym: A squeak from the steering column when turning the wheel.
issues.why: GM bulletin 01-02-35-005 covers this squeak.
issues.next: Mention the bulletin to a shop; the fix is a small adjustment or lubrication.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin
issues.sym: Wet carpets after rain, a musty smell, or water on the floor.
issues.why: Owners report water leaking into the car, including from clogged drains under the hood.
issues.next: Clear the drains at the base of the windshield and under the hood, and have seals checked. Dry the carpet fast to avoid mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Door locks and keyless entry act up
issues.sym: Doors that will not lock or unlock, keyless entry that stops working, or latches that stick.
issues.why: Owners report power lock, door latch and keyless entry failures on these cars.
issues.next: Have the lock actuators and remote checked. A door that will not open from inside needs quick repair.

issues.t: Rear brake squeal
issues.sym: A squeal from the rear brakes when you press the pedal.
issues.why: GM bulletin 97-07-01-75-5004 covers rear brake squeal on the 1997 Catera.
issues.next: Have the rear pads checked and serviced.
